title: Oura API v2 documents (raw)
description: The subset of Oura's API v2 responses that packages/connectors/src/providers/oura reads. Field names are Oura's, not ours. Derived from Oura's own OpenAPI document, spec version 1.37 (https://cloud.ouraring.com/v2/static/json/openapi-1.37.json), read 2026-08-07; the descriptions below quote it. The structural fact that governs this dialect: Oura splits scores from measurements onto different endpoints. daily_sleep is a scorecard with no durations and no heart rate; the night itself is on the sleep endpoint. Every property is optional because Oura types almost all of them as nullable, and a night the ring did not measure arrives with nulls rather than being omitted.

sleep.description: GET /v2/usercollection/sleep — PublicModifiedSleepModel. The measurement document: durations, HRV, heart rate. This is where hrv_ms, sleep_duration_hours and our resting-HR proxy come from.

day.description: Day that the sleep period belongs to, YYYY-MM-DD. Oura's sleep day changes at 6pm, so this is not simply the calendar date of bedtime_start.

type.description: PublicSleepType. Only long_sleep — 'sleep that is long enough (>3h) to automatically contribute to daily scores' — is read as a night. 'sleep' and 'late_nap' are naps of 15 minutes to 3 hours; 'rest' is 'Falsely detected sleep / nap, rejected in confirm prompt by user'; 'deleted' is 'deleted sleep by user'. Counting any of the other four as a night reports more sleep than the athlete had.

total_sleep_duration.description: 'Total sleep duration in seconds.' Seconds, not milliseconds — the unit differs from WHOOP's equivalent.

time_in_bed.description: Seconds in bed. Deliberately not mapped: in-bed time is not sleep time, and total_sleep_duration already reports the latter.

average_hrv.description: 'Average heart rate variability during sleep.' Milliseconds. This is the only millisecond HRV Oura publishes for a night, and the one hrv_ms maps to. It is not hrv_balance, which is a readiness contributor scored in [1, 100].

lowest_heart_rate.description: 'Lowest heart rate during sleep', which the spec notes is computed from 30-second samples. Oura publishes no resting-heart-rate field anywhere, so this is mapped to resting_hr_bpm as our proxy and every emitted reading says so in its metadata.

average_heart_rate.description: Average heart rate during sleep, beats/minute. Not mapped: a night's average is not a resting rate.

efficiency.description: Sleep efficiency rating in range [1, 100]. Not mapped; sleep_quality carries Oura's own daily sleep score instead.

awake_time.description: Seconds awake during the sleep period.

low_battery_alert.description: The ring was low on battery during the period. A reason a night may be sparsely measured.

dailySleep.description: GET /v2/usercollection/daily_sleep — PublicDailySleep. A scorecard, nothing more: id, day, timestamp, score, contributors. It carries no duration and no heart rate, and reading either off it returns undefined.

day.description: 'Day that the daily sleep belongs to.'

score.description: 'Daily sleep score.' Oura's own composite for the night, taken as first-class vendor evidence and never re-derived from the stage durations.

contributors.description: PublicSleepContributors: deep_sleep, efficiency, latency, rem_sleep, restfulness, timing, total_sleep. Every one is documented as 'Contribution of X in range [1, 100]' — the score's own workings, not measurements. Deliberately not read. The registry once mapped the readiness object's hrv_balance out of here as though it were milliseconds; a 1-100 score lands inside the plausible range for HRV in ms, so the error produced numbers a reader would have believed.

temperature_deviation.description: 'Temperature deviation in degrees Celsius.' No canonical home yet.

contributors.description: PublicReadinessContributors: activity_balance, body_temperature, hrv_balance, previous_day_activity, previous_night, recovery_index, resting_heart_rate, sleep_balance, sleep_regularity. All documented as 'Contribution of X in range [1, 100]'. Note that resting_heart_rate here is a contribution score, not a heart rate.

score.description: 'Activity score in range [1, 100].' No canonical home.

workouts.description: GET /v2/usercollection/workout — PublicWorkout. Carries no load figure of any kind: no strain, no TSS, no training load. Oura does not compute one, so normalized workouts arrive with trainingLoad null and are reported through signalCoverage.training.missing rather than given a number derived from duration.

intensity.description: 'Intensity of the workout.' A label, carried as evidence in metadata and never converted into a load number.

calories.description: 'Energy burned in kilocalories during the workout.'

distance.description: 'Distance traveled in meters during the workout.'

source.description: PublicWorkoutSource — which app supplied the workout. Oura is a destination as well as a source.
